description: Folio 1: [? Bedford] to Lt.-Colonel Yorke. Appointing him secretary to the embassy in Paris, to act until the arrival of an ambassador. Date and place: 1749 Jan 16/27 Whitehall.

Folio 2: [? Bedford] to Yorke. Enclosing instructions [not now enclosed] and promising copies of all papers from the Lords Commissioners of Trade about St. Lucia, Tobago and Crown Point, where the French have built a fort on British territory. Date and place: 1749 Jan 17/28 Whitehall.
Folio 4: Bedford to Yorke. He is to inform the French ministers that peace between Britain, France and Spain has been proclaimed in London. Date and place: 1749 Feb 2/13 Whitehall.

Folio 6: Yorke to Bedford. Has arrived in Calais. Two regiments of foot [Rouen and Drummond] are in Calais and one [Albanie, raised for Lochiel] has moved from Calais to Gravelines. Some hundreds of British marines have been recruited from Dover. Date and place: 1749 Feb 10 Calais.
Folio 8: Bedford to Yorke. Asking that France hand over two notorious clippers and coiners - Duff and Davies - who have fled to Boulogne. Date and place: 1749 Feb 6/17 Whitehall.

Folio 10: Yorke to Bedford. Has arrived in Paris and encloses copies of letters arranging a meeting with Puyzieulx at Versailles. Has followed the same form as Durand on his arrival in London. Peace has been proclaimed in Paris. Abolition of some taxes has been announced. Evacuation of the Low Countries said to be completed. Reports the shipwreck on the Normandy coast of British troops destined for Ireland. Cathcart has had reports from Conway's regiment, Murray's and Bragge's. Death of the Dowager Duchess of Orléans. Rumours of troop reductions. Date and place: 1749 Feb 4/15 Paris.
Folio 13: Decree by Conseil d'Etat abolishing taxes imposed in February 1745 and 1748. Date and place: 1749 Feb 4 Versailles.
Folio 14: Royal decree to the Admiral of France, Duc de Penthièvre, laying down rules regarding prizes and neutral shipping during the war. Date and place: 1744 Oct 21 Fribourg.
Folio 15: Decree by Conseil d'Etat abolishing taxes imposed in February 1745 and 1748. Date and place: 1749 Feb 4 Versailles.
Folio 16: Yorke to Puyzieulx. Announcing his arrival. Date and place: 1749 Feb 13 Paris.
Folio 17: Puyzieulx to Yorke. Promising to present him to the King. Sussex and Cathcart will welcome him. Pleased at Durand's cordial reception. Date and place: 1749 Feb 13 Versailles.

Folio 18: Bedford to Yorke. Grateful to Puyzieulx for orders sent to the Intendant of Caen to help the shipwrecked British troops [see f. 10]. Death of the Dowager Duchess of Orléans. Orders to Governor Hopson to hand over Cape Breton will be sent as soon as weather permits. Date and place: 1749 Feb 9/20 Whitehall.

Folio 20: Yorke to Bedford. France refuses to promote the Marquis de Mirepoix to a dukedom to rank with the Duke of Richmond. Puyzieulx asks if Richmond's appointment as ambassador is confirmed. Yorke had made it clear that there was nothing personal against Mirepoix as ambassador. Date and place: 1749 Feb 8/19 Paris.

Folio 23: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting a discussion with Puyzieulx: France would evacuate Hainault, once differences between the Empire and Genoa were settled; he would see Pallavicini, Genoese minister in France, and show Yorke orders sent to Sechelles; France hadno wish that the Pretender's son should remain in Avignon; Puyzieulx favoured Anglo-French co-operation. Yorke had been received by the King and the royal family, as though he had `a character'. Further reference to Genoa (du Theil and Kaunitz are negotiating) and to article 14 of the Definitive Treaty [of Aix-la-Chapelle]. Date and place: 1749 Feb 8/19 Paris.
Folio 31: Bedford to Yorke. Sending letter from the King to the Duc d'Orléans. Reference to Cape Breton. Date and place: 1749 Feb 13/24 Whitehall.
Folio 33: Bedford to Yorke. Yorke is to press concerning the evacuation of Hainault and the Pretender's son in Avignon. Comments on court etiquette. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16/27 Whitehall.
Folio 35: Bedford to Yorke. The King will welcome Mirepoix and is considering the appointment of the ambassador to France. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16/27 Whitehall.
Folio 37: Bedford to Yorke. Enclosing a memorial on behalf of a Mr. Townsend. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16/27 Whitehall.
Folio 39: Memorial from Mr Chauncy Townsend, merchant, concerning the removal of his coal stocks on Cape Breton. Date and place: 1749 nd London.
Folio 40: Note supporting Townsend, who had contracted with the Government to supply coal to Louisbourg. Date and place: 1749 nd London.

Folio 43: Yorke to Bedford. Enclosing letter from Puyzieulx about the evacuation of Hainault and the negotiations between the Empire and Genoa. Holland is still in dispute over the restitution of some artillery. Letters are enclosed from officers of the British troops shipwrecked in Normandy. Yorke praises their discipline. Date and place: 1749 Feb 11/22 Paris.
Folio 45: Puyzieulx to Yorke. Concerning the evacuation of Hainault and the negotiations between the Empire and Genoa. Date and place: 1749 Feb 20 Versailles.
Folio 47: Captain George Scott of Panmure's regiment to Cathcart. Giving details of the shipwreck of British troops in Normandy and their money difficulties. Date and place: 1749 Feb 9 Bernier.
Folio 49: Captain Douglas of Conway's regiment to Yorke. Detailing where troops are quartered, ships aground and the financial needs of the troops. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16 Gray.

Folio 51: Bedford to Yorke. Genoese demands are settled. Gastaldi [Genoese Minister in London] has approached Bedford. The Admiralty will be asked about transports for the shipwrecked troops. Captain Smelt, in the sloop Viper, will sail with orders for the evacuation of Cape Breton. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16/27 Whitehall.

Folio 53: Yorke to Bedford. Referring to Duff and Davies, to rumours of a halt to troop reductions, and to the return to Holland of Major-General Cornabé on the completion of the commission on Dutch prisoners of war. Date and place: 1749 Feb 16/27 Paris.
Folio 55: Yorke to Puyzieulx. Memorial about Duff and Davies. Date and place: 1749 Feb 26 Paris.

Folio 57: Yorke to Bedford. Maurepas [Minister of the Marine] has asked about the embarkation of the shipwrecked British troops. Ministers disagreed about troop reductions. D'Argenson was opposed but had lost, Boscawen is reported in Paris to have retired from Pondicherry. Vaulgrenant leaves for Spain as French ambassador. The Duke of Huescar will return to Madrid. Date and place: 1749 Feb 18/Mar 1 Paris.

Folio 59: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting on a talk with Puyzieulx about Northern Europe. Wishes to improve Anglo-Swedish relations and regrets cool reception to Durand's suggestion. France wants peace but will support Sweden and was disturbed at reported British intention to send a squadron to the Baltic. Yorke has assured him that British troop reductions would continue. Date and place: 1749 Feb 18/Mar 1 Paris.
Folio 65: Bedford to Yorke. Concerning Duff and Davies. Date and place: 1749 Feb 23/Mar 6 Whitehall.
Folio 67: Bedford to Yorke. The Earl of Albemarle has been appointed Ambassador to France. Date and place: 1749 Feb 27/Mar 10 Whitehall.

note: Part to be sent in cipher. Separate.
description: Folio 69: Bedford to Yorke. Referring to f. 59, states that the British ministers in Vienna and Moscow have been ordered to stress the need to avoid any disturbance in Northern Europe when the King of Sweden dies. He refers to Prussian armaments and asserts that the retention by Britain of 3000 seamen is to avoid pressing and is similar to the retention of soldiers in the French militia. Date and place: 1749 Feb 27/Mar 10 Whitehall

Folio 73: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting that the Pretender's son has left Avignon because the Pope fears British action. His wherabouts are unknown. The lifting of the Dixième is expected. There is unrest over the troop reductions. Date and place: 1749 Feb 25/Mar 8 Paris.

Folio 75: Yorke to Bedford. Two transports and the sloop Scorpion have arrived to embark the shipwrecked British troops for the Isle of Wight. Encloses Royal Ordinances for troop reductions. Date and place: 1749 Feb 22/Mar 5 Paris.
Folio 77: Royal Ordinance concerning some German Infantry regiments. Date and place: 1749 Feb 1 Versailles.
Folio 79: Royal Ordinance concerning French Infantry regiments. Date and place: 1749 Feb 9 Versailles.

Folio 85: Yorke to Bedford. Reports that Puyzieulx, encouraged by Schaeffer [Baron Scheffer], fears an alliance in Northern Europe between Britain, Denmark and Russia, and suspects Anglo-Dutch solidarity. His reputation is at stake if war breaks out. Date and place: 1749 Feb 25/Mar 8 Paris.

note: Part to be sent in cipher.
description: Folio 88: Bedford to Yorke. Good conduct of shipwrecked troops. Yorke is to investigate report that Tobago has been granted to Saxe. Date and place: 1749 Mar 2/13 Whitehall.
Folio 90: Bedford to Yorke. Good conduct of shipwrecked troops. Yorke is to investigate report that Tobago has been granted to Saxe. Date and place: 1749 Mar 2/13 Whitehall.
Folio 92: Yorke to Bedford. The Townsend papers have been referred to Maurepas [see ff. 39 and 40]. Refers to the Pretender's son and to Duff and Davies. Date and place: 1749 Mar 1/12 Paris.

Folio 94: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting a conversation with Puyzieulx on Northern Europe and Puyzieulx' unwillingness to evict the Pretender's son by force from Papal territory [Avignon]. Date and place: 1749 Mar 4/15 Paris.

Folio 99: Yorke to Bedford. No news of Duff and Davies. Report about Tobago and Saxe is denied. Saxe said to be going to Poland to claim Duchy of Courland. The King is at Choisy. Belle-Isle has arrived from Italy. The stock-market is rising on news from the East Indies. Date and place: 1749 Mar 4/15 Paris.
Folio 101: Bedford to Yorke. Acknowledging letters. Date and place: 1749 Mar 9/20 Whitehall.
Folio 103: Yorke to Bedford. Albermarle's appointment is welcomed. The answer about Townsend is enclosed. Tobago has been refused to Saxe. Date and place: 1749 Mar 8/20 Paris.
Folio 105: Reply to Townsend memorial [f. 39].

note: Part to be sent in cipher.
description: Folio 107: Bedford to Yorke. Declarations by Durand that the Pretender's son would be sent to Civita Vecchia if found in France and that France wanted peace in Northern Europe. Bedford refers to British declarations in Vienna and Moscow [see f. 69]. In view of her treatment of Colonel Dickens, Sweden must make first move towards an exchange of ministers. No British squadron will be sent to the Baltic. Date and place: 1749 Mar 13/24 Whitehall.

note: Part to be sent in cipher.
description: Folio 112: Bedford to Yorke. The Earl of Halifax has an eye-witness report of document appointing a Lt. Governor to Tobago and signed by Saxe. Le Touche [? La Touche] connected with Saxe. Date and place: 1749 Mar 13/24 Whitehall.

Folio 114: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx denies any grant to Saxe in America, but cites Treaty of Nijmegen in reply to British claim to Tobago. Incident in which Caylus had stopped a ship dispatched by the Governor of Barbados to St. Lucia and St Vincent. Encloses a letter from de Froulay, Maltese ambassador to France [not now enclosed] and a pamphlet about the Dixième being distributed in Paris. Refers to disturbances in Bordeaux and the British withdrawal from Pondicherry. Date and place: 1749 Mar 11/22 Paris.
Folio 116: Pamphlet attacking the Dixième. Date and place: 1749 [? Mar] Paris.

Folio 118: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting on discussion with Puyzieulx on Northern Europe. Count Tessin is mentioned in connection with a plot. Yorke suspicious of Prussian arms. A report about the Pretender's son. Date and place: 1749 Mar 11/22 Paris.
Folio 124: Bedford to Yorke. Acknowledging letters. Date and place: 1749 Mar 16/27 Whitehall.

Folio 126: Bedford to Yorke. Reporting the declaration by Count Zoehrern, Imperial Minister in London, of the Empire's peaceful intentions, contrary to Prussian rumours. Puyzieulx to be asked to warn Prussia against `raising a flame in the North'. Date and place: 1749 Mar 20/31 Whitehall.

Folio 130: Yorke to Bedford. Refers to Duff and Davies and the Young Pretender. Finkenstein expected from Berlin. The pamphlet against the Dixième [f. 116] has been burnt by the common hangman. The Duc de Chevreuse is probably to be appointed ambassador to the Empire The Marquis de Vaulgrenant leaves for Spain. Valori on his way back to Berlin. Date and place: 1749 Mar 15/26 Paris.

Folio 132: Bedford to Yorke. Enclosing copies of accounts [not enclosed here: enclosed with letter from Lords Commissioners of Trade, Apr. 1] from Mr Sharpe, agent for Barbados. French claim to Tobago is based on its capture from the Dutch in the reign of Louis XIVand on the Treaty of Nijmegen Bedford argues that the Duke of Courland, who held Tobago under Britain, was driven out by rebels, who were defeated by the French; the Treaty of Nijmegen therefore does not apply. French activities in St. Vincent, St. Lucia and Dominica and on Tobago as reported by Captain Wheeler of H.M.S. Boston. Yorke is to ask Maurepas what orders have been issued to French captains and to affirm Britain's intention to defend her rights in Tobago. Date and place: 1749 Mar 23/Apr 3 Whitehall.

Folio 138: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting on a talk with Puyzieulx about Northern Europe, Prussian arms and Swedish links with Turkey. Mentions Franco-Dutch commerce, plotting in Amsterdam against the Prince of Orange, and the removal of a levy per ton on British shipping. Date and place: 1749 Mar 8/29 Paris.
Folio 142: Yorke to Bedford. Concerning correspondence. Date and place: 1749 Mar 22/Apr 2 Paris.

Folio 144: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting talk with Puyzieulx on Northern Europe. Prussia fears an attack. Blondel to warn the Empire against aggression. Scheffer says that Sweden will nominate a Minister to Britain other than Carlson, who had made himself unacceptable when in Constantinople. Date and place: 1749 Mar 25/Apr 5 Paris.

Folio 148: Yorke to Bedford. Maurepas will co-operate over Cape Breton. Yorke is convinced that Saxe, who is leaving for Dresden, has not been granted patent for Tobago. Rumours about the Young Pretender. Date and place: 1749 Mar 25/Apr 5 Paris.
Folio 150: Bedford to Yorke. Informing him that the ship carrying orders to hand over Louisbourg will sail shortly. Date and place: 1749 Mar 30/Apr 10 Whitehall.
Folio 152: Aldworth [Under Secretary, Southern Province] to Yorke. The King is unwell. Date and place: 1749 Apr 3/14 Whitehall.

Folio 154: Bedford to Yorke. Enclosing copies [not now enclosed] of a letter from Grenville, a petition to Grenville and an ordinance by Caylus, brought from Tobago by Captain Tyrell of H.M.S. Chesterfield. Yorke is to ask Puyzieulx to repudiate Caylus' actions, toprovide copies of orders issued to Caylus and to take note of the agreement of 1730, neutralizing St. Vincent, St. Lucia and Dominica. He is to ask if the French ship Junon carried orders to Caylus. Date and place: 1749 Apr 4/15 Whitehall.

Folio 158: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting on an interview with Puyzieulx about Tobago. He pressed to know if Montal, captain of the Junon, had been handed orders for Caylus. Puyzieulx defended Caylus and criticised Grenville. Reference to the neutral islands. Rumour about the Pretender's son. Date and place: 1749 Mar 29/Apr 9 Paris.

Folio 162: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx awaits Russia's reaction to Zoehrer's declaration [see f. 126], and criticises presence of Russian troops on Sweden's Finnish frontier. Prussia seeks guarantees under article 22 of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle. Yorke had claimed that Prussia could not invoke article 22 without accepting article 23. Puyzieulx was going to communicate with Prussia through Chambrier. Date and place: 1749 Apr 1/12 Paris.
Folio 166: Yorke to Bedford. He will hand to Maurepas memorials about Montal and Tobago. Date and place: 1749 Apr 1/12 Paris.

Folio 168: Yorke to Bedford. Enclosing copies of memorials mentioned in f. 166 [not now enclosed]. Maurepas claimed that the French were under orders to abide by the preliminaries to the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle but that Grenville had been provocative. He wanted all disputes in the West Indies and [North] America settled by Commissaries. Yorke had agreed subject to the status quo being restored. Finkenstein has arrived. Date and place: 1749 Apr 5/16 Paris.

note: Part to be sent in cipher.
description: Folio 172: Bedford to Yorke. Concerning Prussia and Northern Europe. Reference to the West Indies. Date and place: 1749 Apr 10/21 Whitehall.

note: see f. 168. Part to be sent in cipher. Separate.
description: Folio 175: Bedford to Yorke. Britain will not withdraw her claim to Tobago and will consider question of appointing Commissaries. Date and place: 1749 Apr 10/21 Whitehall
Folio 177: Yorke to Bedford. The Bishop of Rennes [Guérapin de Vauréal] has been banished from Court for failing to check British influence in Spain. Date and place: 1749 Apr 8/19 Paris.

Folio 179: Yorke to Bedford. Encloses reply [not now enclosed] to the two memorials [see f. 166]. Puyzieulx defends Montal, criticises Tyrrell and denies that the Junon carried orders to settle in Tobago. Maurepas has handed Yorke copies of all orders sent to Caylus [not now enclosed]. De la Chétardie to be ambassador in Turin. Huescar has left for Madrid. The Prince d'Ardore [di Ardore], ambassador to France from the Two Sicilies, has left for Naples. Date and place: 1749 Apr 12/23 Paris.

Folio 182: Yorke to Bedford. Maurepas has been banished to Bourges. His enemies include "the Lady" [? Madame de Pompadour], [? Comte] d'Argenson and Richelieu. Yorke lists possible successors Rumours about the Young Pretender. Encloses a letter [not now enclosed] from the King of Poland, Duc de Lorraine, to the King of England. Date and place: 1749 Apr 15/26 Paris.
Folio 185: Bedford to Yorke. The King has recovered. Date and place: 1749 Apr 20/May 1 Whitehall.
Folio 187: Yorke to Aldworth, The Court is moving to Marli. Rouillé [Counsellor of State] succeeds Maurepas as Minister of the Marine. Date and place: 1749 Apr 19/30 Paris.
Folio 189: Yorke to Bedford. He has discussed Northern Europe with Puyzieulx. Finkenstein has achieved nothing. Yorke has denied rumours of delays over Cape Breton.

Folio 192: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx had admitted that Caylus went too far and advised against a memorial to Maurepas over the neutral islands, implying his opposition to him. French ships for Canada delayed by an accident at Brest. The Young Pretender is rumoured to be dead. Date and place: 1749 Apr 22/May 3 Paris.

Folio 195: Yorke to Bedford. The Vingtième will probably be imposed to make up for the abolition of the Dixième. An allocation is expected for the fleet. Twenty-five warships are said to be on the stocks. Mirepoix is ready to leave for London. Yorke is being asked when Albemarle will depart. Date and place: 1749 Apr 26/May 7 Paris.
Folio 197: Yorke to Aldworth. Listing expected taxes. The Parliament is likely to protest. The Duke of Modena is leaving for London. Date and place: 1749 Apr 29/May 10 Paris.

Folio 199: Yorke to Bedford. Jacobites are spreading rumours of unrest in London and Oxford. Probable sources are Monsieur de Guilles [d' Aiguilles], French Minister to the Young Pretender, captured at Culloden, and General Buckley. Reference to the arrest of Colonel Kennedy and to Brigadier Lally. Date and place: 1749 Apr 30/May 9 [?11] Paris.

Folio 202: Bedford to Yorke. He is to insist that the case of the three neutral islands - St. Vincent, St. Lucia and Dominica -, which rests on the agreement of 1730, must be taken separately from that of Tobago, which can be discussed as soon as the status quo there is restored. Copies of orders to West Indian governors should be exchanged. Date and place: 1749 May 8/19 Whitehall.

note: To be sent in cipher. Separate and private.
description: Folio 207: Bedford to Yorke. He is to sound Puyzieulx about a convention to preserve the neutrality of the four islands - St. Vincent, St. Lucia, Dominica and Tobago. Date and place: 1749 May 8/19 Whitehall.

Folio 210: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx has reported Swedish regret at the non-acceptance of Carlson. Baron Hamilton has been nominated as Minister to Britain. Rumours about the Pretender's son, an impending protest from Puyzieulx at the establishment of a colony inNova Scotia and the return soon to Berlin of Finkenstein. The Dauphine has had a miscarriage. Date and place: 1749 May 3/14 Paris.

Folio 212: Bedford to Yorke. Neither Hamilton nor any member "of a certain set of men" would be acceptable as Minister from Sweden. Puyzieulx' attitude to the Young Pretender is appreciated. Nova Scotia does not concern France. Date and place: 1749 May 11/22 Whitehall.
Folio 215: Bedford to Yorke. Enclosing a translation of a memorial from Zoehrern and an extract from a dispatch from Hyndford. Date and place: 1749 May 14/25 Woburn Abbey.

Folio 217: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx has reported accounts of the movements of the Pretender's son from the Marquis des Issarts, French ambassador in Saxony, and a conversation between Sir Charles Hanbury Williams and Count Bruehl. Puyzieulx has ordered all French representatives, including Perron de Castera in Poland, to have nothing to do with him. Date and place: 1749 May 6/17 Paris.

Folio 219: Yorke to Bedford. Refers to intrigues around the Bishop of Rennes. D'Argenson has arrested someone for spreading libels. Parliament is opposed to the tax edicts. Finkenstein leaves, having gained little. Date and place: 1749 May 6/17 Paris.

Folio 221: Yorke to Aldworth. Parliament has protested to the King about the Vingtième. The Marquis d'Havrincourt succeeds the Marquis Lanmarie as Minister to Sweden. Date and place: 1749 May 10/21 Paris.

Folio 223: Yorke to Bedford. Enclosing two Royal Edicts; one for imposing the Vingtième in place of the Dixième and one for raising thirty six million livres on 5% annuities. Postscript mentions Puyzieulx' silence on Nova Scotia. Date and place: 1749 May 13/24 Paris.
Folio 225: Royal edict on raising money through annuities. Date and place: 1749 May Marli.
Folio 227: Royal edict, establishing the Vingtième and abolishing the Dixième. Date and place: 1749 May Marli.

Folio 231: Yorke to Bedford. A discussion with Puyzieulx on the West Indies. Puyzieulx is unwilling to negotiate over Tobago and the three neutral islands separately, and does not accept the British interpretation of Article 9 of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle. He will exchange orders [see f. 202], if Britain will appoint a Commissary. He regrets the rejection of Hamilton. Rouillé says that orders have been sent to Caylus to observe the treaty. Date and place: 1749 May 20/31 Paris.

Folio 235: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx has agreed to exchange duplicate orders, if Britain appoints a Commissary [see ff. 202 and 231], Yorke believes that France is maintaining her claims to Tobago to bargain over Nova Scotia. Date and place: 1749 May 20/31 Paris.

Folio 237: Yorke to Bedford. The Pretender's son cannot be far from Paris; delivery of letters to Walters the banker and General Buckley [Bulkeley] suggests this. D'Argenson has tried to find him. Puyzieulx has sent orders to the West Indies and refers again to theappointment of a commissary. Date and place: 1749 May 24/June 4 Paris.

Folio 241: Bedford to Yorke. Britain insists on negotiating separately over Tobago, but will appoint commissaries to attend Albemarle and will exchange duplicate orders to evacuate all four islands. Date and place: 1749 June 1/12 Whitehall.

Folio 243: Yorke to Aldworth. Asking him to send samples of tin and copper ore for the collection of a friend who is Inspector of the Royal Cabinet of Natural Curiosities. Date and place: 1749 May 27/June 7 Paris.

Folio 245: Bedford to Yorke. Sending extracts [not now enclosed] from two letters from Boscawen to the Admiralty, showing how long it had taken for orders to end hostilities to reach the East Indies. Date and place: 1749 June 5/16 Whitehall.

Folio 247: Yorke to Bedford. Further reports about the Pretender's son. France will not support those in French service who act in his support and is grateful for the release of Brigadier Kennedy. Yorke reports a discussion with Rouillé about the West Indies. St. Lucia seems to be a special French interest. Puyzieulx' Memorial on Nova Scotia will be delivered by Durand. The Marquis d'Hautefort is to be French ambassador in Vienna. Saxe has left for Dresden. Date and place: 1749 May 31/June 11 Paris.
Folio 251: Bedford to Yorke. Durand has presented the memorial on Nova Scotia. Date and place: 1749 June 8/19 Whitehall.

Folio 253: Yorke to Bedford. Puyzieulx thinks the Pretender's son is in Venice. The Court is moving to Marli, then to Compiègne. Count Chavannes [Sardinian envoy to Holland] is en route to Turin. Count Ossorio [Sardinian ambassador to Spain] is leaving for Madrid. Date and place: 1749 June 3/14 Paris.
Folio 255: Yorke to Bedford. Three of Mirepoix' four chaplains are Irish priests. Date and place: 1749 June 3/14 Paris.

Folio 257: Bedford to Yorke. Enclosing an extract [not now enclosed] of a letter from Keith, outlining the Empire's reaction to Yorke's stand in f. 162. Yorke is to maintain his stand on Article 23 of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, if Prussia presses Article 22. Date and place: 1749 June 12/23 Whitehall.

note: Part to be sent in cipher Separate.
description: Folio 259: Bedford to Yorke. He is to protest at the French stirring up jealousies over Northern Europe in Constantinople, aided by the Swedish minister. Keith has praised Blondel's conduct in the face of protests from Count Uhlfeldt. Date and place: 1749 June 12/23 Whitehall.
Folio 261: Yorke to Bedford. The Pretender's son has settled in Bologna. His servants have left Avignon. Reference to Bulkeley. Date and place: 1749 June 7/18 Paris.

Folio 263: Yorke to Bedford. Lady Mary Herbert has asked him to help in the case of her niece, Miss Herbert, a ward in Chancery, in a convent in Paris, who may be influenced to move away, against the wishes of her relations. Date and place: 1749 June 10/21 Paris.

Folio 265: Memorial from Lady Mary Herbert to Yorke. Explaining how her niece came under the guardianship of Lady Mountacute [Montagu], who wants her to marry her son, when she comes of age. Date and place: 1749 June 20 Paris.
Folio 267: Yorke to Puyzieulx. Asking his help in the case of Miss Herbert. Date and place: 1749 June 20 Paris.

Folio 269: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting a talk with Puyzieulx about the West Indies. France agrees to negotiate separately over Tobago and to move the Commissaries from St. Malo to another town [see SP 78/234]. Honours to be paid to Albemarle and Mirepoix are mentioned. The Comte de Chavigni may go as French envoy to Venice. Date and place: 1749 June 14/25 Paris.

Folio 272: Yorke to Bedford. Reporting on duties levied on British ships in French ports. Cites the case of Keadie and has referred Puyzieulx to articles in the treaties of Utrecht and Aix-la-Chapelle. Date and place: 1749 June 14/25 Paris.

Folio 275: Action by Captain Keadie of the British ship Good Intention, against Monsieur Thibault Larue, Adjudicator General of Taxes, countersigned by Gaspord Imbert, Sheriff's officer of Cette [? Sète, Mediterranean]. Date and place: 1749 May 22 Cette.

note: Part to be sent in cipher.
description: Folio 277: Bedford to Yorke. Advising caution in the Herbert case, lest her Catholic relations try to keep her from her Protestant ones. Date and place: 1749 June 22/July 3 Whitehall.

Folio 279: Yorke to Bedford. He has protested to Puyzieulx over the activity of Desalleurs in Turkey [see f. 259]. Unpleasantness for British travellers at Calais from Scotch-French regiments stationed there. Puyzieulx has agreed to move them. The Court is to move to Compiègne. Date and place: 1749 June 21/July 2 Paris.
